ex.s: This is how everyone learned to read． We would start off with sentences， then paragraphs， and then stories． It seemed an unending journey， but even as a six﹣year﹣old girl I realized that knowing how to read could open many doors． When mom said， "The C﹣A﹣N﹣D﹣Y is hidden on the top shelf，" I knew where the candy was． My progress in reading raised my curiosity， and I wanted to know everything． I often found myself telling my mom to drive more slowly， so that I could read all of the road signs we passed．
ex.t: 每个人都是这样学会阅读的。我们从句子开始，然后是段落，再然后是故事。这似乎是一段永无止境的旅程，但即使作为一个六岁的女孩，我也意识到学会阅读能打开许多扇门。当妈妈说：“C-A-N-D-Y藏在最上面的架子上”时，我知道糖果在哪里。我在阅读上的进步激发了我的好奇心，我想知道一切。我经常叫妈妈开慢一点，这样我就能读出我们路过的所有路标。

ex.s: The good news is that there is evidence we can learn to change our own story.
ex.t: 好消息是，有证据表明我们可以学会改写自己的人生故事。

ex.s: Keep interesting magazine pictures to give children story ideas.
ex.t: 保留有趣的杂志图片，给孩子们提供故事创意。

ex.s: In this book, I tell a story of these assumptions.
ex.t: 在这本书里，我讲述了这些预设的故事。

ex.s: This includes, but is not limited to: visual art, graphic art, photography, poetry, short story, non-fiction, etc Submissions may be from existing or newly created work.
ex.t: 包括但不限于：视觉艺术、平面艺术、摄影、诗歌、短篇小说、非虚构作品等。投稿可以是已有作品或新创作的作品。

ex.s: And you might find it relaxing to bring your small kid to a half-hour Story Time while you sit quietly in a corner with a good book.
ex.t: 你可能觉得带着小孩去半小时的“故事时间”很放松，而你可以安静地坐在角落里读一本好书。

ex.s: Our life story is something that starts coming together in our teenage years, when we begin to organise our lives into chapters around key events or life changes, and begin to see ourselves as both the central character and, to a varying extent, the story’s author.
ex.t: 我们的人生故事在青少年时期开始成形，那时我们开始把生活围绕关键事件或人生变化整理成一个个章节，并开始把自己视为故事的中心人物，并且在不同程度上也视为这个故事的创作者。

ex.s: In looking into the stories of biological discovery, I also began to find something else, a collection of scientists, usually brilliant occasionally half-mad, who made the discoveries.
ex.t: 第二个抽屉也开始填满了，当它填满时我在想是否还有更大的发现，不仅仅是物种，还有依赖于被认为无用的东西的生命，甚至是没有DNA的生命。

ex.s: However, psychologists have demonstrated that when adults read news stories, they remember more of the content than if they listen to or view identical pieces.
ex.t: 然而，心理学家已经证明，当成年人阅读新闻故事时，比起聆听或观看相同的片段，他们对内容的记忆更多。

ex.s: If it’s short stories, Peter Mountford breaks down six techniques you can try to see which one helps you stick the landing.
ex.t: 如果是短篇小说，彼得·蒙特福德拆解了六种技巧，你可以试试看哪种能帮你完美收官。

ex.s: “We wanted to do something where we do a call to artists in the Bay Area to submit stories for a contest,” Trost says.
ex.t: 我们想做点什么，向湾区的艺术家征集故事来参赛，”Trost说。

ex.s: So I absolutely think we will get more riders just because of short stories,” she says.
ex.t: 所以我绝对相信，仅因为短篇故事我们就会迎来更多乘客，”她说。

ex.s: What does Nielsen’s career story tell us?
ex.t: 尼尔森的职业生涯告诉我们什么？

a report in a newspaper, magazine or news broadcast 新闻报道

ex.s: When your boss or professor sends you out to do man-on-the-street interviews for a story, think about the topic and develop a list of about ten general questions relating to it.
ex.t: 当你的老板或教授派你出去为一篇报道做街头采访时，先想想主题，并就此列出大约十个相关问题。
